rows.description: The one left behind feels a dull ache and wonders what he did. Children rarely explain a drift, so the hurt one may assume rejection when the real cause is only busier days and new company.
graph_context: previous stage: Changing interests and groups
next stage: Keeping kindness through change
this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22
related mind states: curiosity, awe, hurt

rows.description: A parent helps the child say hello, invite the old friend to one game, and accept that friends can be different for different seasons. Loss is real, but it does not mean the friendship was false.
graph_context: previous stage: Fading without a fight
this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22

rows.description: In a hostel or first job city, a young adult lonely and eager says yes to every invitation. Shared meals, late-night chats and mutual homesickness create quick intimacy that feels stronger than it yet is.
graph_context: next stage: Deepening through disclosure
this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12
related mind states: excitement, loneliness, nostalgia

rows.description: They tell each other family troubles, fears about careers and old heartbreaks. Reciprocal self-disclosure is what makes a friendship real, and each is measuring whether the other responds with care.
graph_context: previous stage: New environment, open door
next stage: Routine and a core group
this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12
related mind states: fear

rows.subtype: Stage 3: Routine and a core group [Observer]
rows.description: An outsider sees the group eating, studying and travelling together and taking it for granted. The comfort is real, but so is the unspoken pressure to stay in the group and not seek other friends.
graph_context: previous stage: Deepening through disclosure
next stage: Divergence
this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12

rows.description: One friend gets a placement in another city, another falls into a relationship, a third struggles with money. Calls turn into likes on posts, and both feel guilty for being the one who did not call.
graph_context: previous stage: Routine and a core group
next stage: Fading and quiet grief
this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12
related mind states: guilt

rows.description: One realises months have passed since a real conversation and feels sadness with no single event to blame. Ordinary fading is easy to overlook, and it can hurt like a loss without permission to mourn.
graph_context: previous stage: Divergence
next stage: Choosing what to keep
this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12
related mind states: sadness, grief, hurt

rows.description: Instead of waiting for the old closeness, one sends a specific message like "I was thinking of our Sunday chai. Can we talk this weekend?" Some ties deserve effort; others can be let go with thanks.
graph_context: previous stage: Fading and quiet grief
this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12

rows.subtopic: Friendship betrayal to reconciliation or ending
